A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from BayesianVLA to LangForce. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including v1 Appendix A and v6 Appendices A–C.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision-only pilot experiments, SimplerEnv and RoboCasa evaluations, component ablations, and qualitative language-generation results.

after.justification: v6 retains original simulation experiments and reports additional LIBERO comparisons, physical-robot experiments, diagnostic measurements, and ablations.

M1.justification: The shared dual-branch architecture, 64 action queries, LLR and flow-matching objectives, and posterior-only inference remain. Section 3.3 newly specifies detaching prior-query features when optimizing the prior action loss. Because v1 does not specify this gradient path, the PDFs do not establish whether this changes the procedure or documents an existing implementation choice.

E1.justification: v6 adds physical Franka evaluations involving colored blocks, unseen colors, multiple target blocks, distractors, and four vegetables, plus broader OXE pretraining coverage described in Table 8. LIBERO already appeared in v1's pilot experiments, so its expanded results are not wholly new task coverage. RoboTwin was named and planned in v1 without reported experimental evidence; its omission does not establish removed evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: SimplerEnv Table 1 removes RT-1-X, Octo-Small, and OpenVLA and adds Magma. RoboCasa adds Isaac-GR00T N1.5. LIBERO expands from the vision-only/full-model pilot comparison to comparisons including OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, π0, π0.5, QwenFAST, and QwenOFT (v6 Table 6). Appendix B.4 also introduces an auxiliary-language-prediction comparator.

E3.justification: SimplerEnv training changes from 40k steps on 16 GPUs to 50k on 8, retaining batch size 16 per device; RoboCasa follows these settings. The pilot description changes language masking from evaluation to training. These are reported protocol revisions, without establishing reruns. New protocols include physical-robot trials and a 40,000-sample NLL/PPL analysis; LIBERO additionally specifies Avg@500 evaluation.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's baseline/query/full-model ablation, v6 adds separate λ and β sweeps, including zero-weight controls, a 16–128 query-count study, and auxiliary language-prediction controls with qualitative examples. It also adds the LIBERO Goal NLL/PPL diagnostic and physical tests of unseen colors, multiple targets, and distractors. These investigate component contributions, mechanisms, and robustness previously untested in the reported evidence.

E5.justification: v6 Table 7 introduces NLL standard deviations of 0.55 and 0.54 for its diagnostic analysis. Existing Avg@480 and Avg@50 reporting remains. Neither version supplies training-seed variability, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests; the new standard deviations do not establish additional independent training runs.

E6.justification: The proposed method's SimplerEnv average remains 66.5%, but Table 1 revises OpenVLA-OFT from 23.4% to 41.8%, π0 from 27.1% to 53.1%, and QwenGR00T's eggplant score from 64.2% to 54.2%. RoboCasa's proposed-method average changes from 50.4% to 52.6% under revised reported settings. The full-model ablation changes from 63.5% to 66.5%. Extensive LIBERO, real-world, and diagnostic results are added. These updates do not establish same-setting improvements between versions.

T1.justification: The conditional-information bound, Bayesian identities, LLR derivation, and flow-matching equations are mathematically retained. Appendix A is rewritten without a new derivation or proof. The world-model factorization moves from v1's discussion to v6 Appendix C. The NLL/PPL diagnostic adds empirical measurement and interpretation, not new formal theory.

C1.justification: The central vision-shortcut diagnosis and Bayesian training contribution remain. v6's conclusion extends its empirical claim to LIBERO and physical pick-and-place and replaces v1's sweeping statement about standard methods failing completely with comparative improvement claims. Its introduction changes the headline SimplerEnv improvement from 11.3% to 8.8%, although the abstract and Section 4.1 retain 11.3%, creating an inconsistency.

C2.justification: v6 adds substantive interpretations connecting auxiliary-language controls and loss-weight ablations to action-relevant grounding, and interprets higher NLL/PPL as preserved task uncertainty. It distinguishes training-loss evidence from downstream execution and argues that physical-test benefits concern instruction following more than motor control. New limitations explicitly exclude validation of dexterous/contact-rich manipulation. The earlier multimodal-degradation and training-overhead caveats are retained, not newly introduced.

D1.justification: v6 discloses default λ=0.3 and β=0.1, explains query-embedding expansion and prior-feature detachment, and substantially documents physical experiments: Franka Research 3, RealSense D435, Polymetis, end-effector pose control, demonstrations per color/vegetable, held-out red blocks, and distractors. Table 8 identifies 20 OXE subsets, robot platforms, and episode counts. These materially expand reproducibility information beyond v1.

R1.justification: v1 positions Bayesian decomposition mainly against architectural or scaling approaches. v6 explicitly acknowledges BayesVLA as another Bayesian approach and distinguishes LangForce's single-stage training from its described frozen-prior, two-stage procedure. This materially refines positioning against a close predecessor. Related work also expands discussion of TwinBrainVLA, adds 3D-Mix and shortcut-learning literature, and removes Octo; StarVLA's bibliographic update represents the same work.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the method, v6 substantially reorganizes the narrative: related work precedes discussion, detailed discussion moves to Appendix C, capability-preservation material moves into Appendix B.4, and limitations precede a rewritten conclusion. Method explanations are expanded, several sections are condensed or rewritten, and acknowledgements and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from single-column to two-column layout. RoboCasa's full table becomes an appendix table with grouped averages, accompanied by a compact main-text summary. New tables and Figures 6–9 display controls, diagnostics, dataset composition, domain differences, and physical rollouts. Figure 5 is relocated to the appendix; the original principal diagrams and qualitative examples remain.

improvement.justification: v6 substantially strengthens two weaknesses of v1: physical validation existed only as a plan, and component analysis could not distinguish the full objective from simpler language-retention training. Real-robot comparisons and the auxiliary-language, zero-weight, and query-count controls provide consequential new evidence, supported by much better implementation documentation. These gains outweigh remaining weaknesses: the introduction's 8.8% conflicts with 11.3% elsewhere, ablation prose still reports 63.5% despite Table 5's 66.5%, and higher NLL alone does not establish the claimed entropy mechanism. The improvement lies in stronger empirical scrutiny and reproducibility, not simply more results.
